title: Locally constant finite type sheaves form a weak Serre subcategory
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and $B$ a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. The full subcategory of sheaves of $\underline B$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] which are locally constant of finite type is closed under kernels and cokernels of morphisms between its objects, and under extensions in the abelian category of sheaves of $\underline B$-modules. Here $\underline B$ is the constant sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]; locally constant of finite type means that locally on the site the sheaf is isomorphic to the constant sheaf associated to a finitely generated $B$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. No existence of points of the site is assumed.

proof.text: Fix any object $U$. To test local constancy, work on $\mathcal C/U$, whose final object is $U\to U$. Trivialize both sheaves by successive coverings and bind the covers using the site axioms. Relocalization identifies the resulting slices with $\mathcal C/V$. Restriction preserves kernels because they are sectionwise. It preserves epimorphisms: for a section over $V/U$, the general-site epimorphism theorem supplies a covering of $V$ and local lifts, and that same covering is a covering of $V/U$ in the slice. The faithful exact forgetful functor identifies module-sheaf exactness with underlying abelian-sheaf exactness. Thus restriction preserves short exact sequences and hence kernels and cokernels in these abelian categories. The canonical restriction comparison identifies further restrictions of constants with constants. Thus for the kernel and cokernel problem we may assume the two sheaves are $\underline M,\underline N$ with $M,N$ finitely generated.

Apply the local-morphism lemma to $\varphi:\underline M\to\underline N$. On every nondegenerate member of its covering sieve it becomes $\underline f$ for a linear map $f:M\to N$. Sectionwise exactness of the constant-module functor applied to $0\to\ker f\to M\to\operatorname{im}f\to0$ and $0\to\operatorname{im}f\to N\to\operatorname{coker}f\to0$ identifies the kernel and cokernel sheaves with $\underline{\ker f}$ and $\underline{\operatorname{coker}f}$. The Noetherian submodule theorem makes $\ker f$ finitely generated. Images of generators of $N$ generate $\operatorname{coker}f$. On an object covered by the empty sieve every sheaf has only the zero section, so its restriction is the zero constant module and already satisfies the desired conclusion. These local descriptions prove both closure clauses without assuming points.

Now start with $0\to\mathcal F\xrightarrow{i}\mathcal E\xrightarrow{p}\mathcal G\to0$ and restrict first to each member of a cover trivializing $\mathcal F$, and then to the members of a cover trivializing $\mathcal G$. Cover composition and relocalization identify these restrictions with slices of the original site. The sectionwise-kernel and local-surjectivity argument of step 1 gives exact restriction, including for module sheaves by the exact forgetful functor; hence the short exact module sequence remains short exact on each slice. The constant-restriction comparisons write its outer terms as $\underline M$ and $\underline N$, with $M,N$ finitely generated. Choose finitely many generators $y_1,\ldots,y_t$ of $N$, define $q:B^t\twoheadrightarrow N$, and put $K=\ker q$. The Noetherian submodule theorem applied to $B^t$ gives finite generation of $K$. Sectionwise constant exactness gives $0\to\underline K\to\underline{B^t}\xrightarrow{\underline q}\underline N\to0$. This includes $t=0$ when $N=0$.

The underlying abelian-sheaf map $p$ is epic, since the exact forgetful functor preserves its cokernel. By the general-site epimorphism theorem each of the finitely many constant generator sections $y_j$ lifts locally to a section $s_j$ of $\mathcal E$. Successively refine these finitely many coverings; restriction and relocalization preserve all previously obtained lifts. The formula $\ell(a_1,\ldots,a_t)=\sum_j a_js_j$ defines a module-sheaf map $\ell:\underline{B^t}\to\mathcal E$ with $p\ell=\underline q$: first define it on the constant presheaf, then extend uniquely by the constant sheafification universal property. Equality follows by checking the free generators. For $t=0$ no refinement is necessary.

Since $p\ell|_{\underline K}=0$, the kernel property gives $g:\underline K\to\underline M$ with $ig=\ell|_{\underline K}$. Define $a:\underline K\to\underline M\oplus\underline{B^t}$ by $a(k)=(-g(k),k)$ and $b(m,v)=i(m)+\ell(v)$. Then $ba=0$. Every section $e$ of $\mathcal E$ is locally in the image of $b$: lift $p(e)$ along $\underline q$ (the constant sequence is even sectionwise exact), subtract $\ell(v)$ and use $\ker p=\underline M$. Conversely, if $b(m,v)=0$, then $q(v)=0$, so $v$ is a section of $\underline K$ and injectivity of $i$ gives $m=-g(v)$. Thus $\ker b=\operatorname{im}a$ and $b$ is epic by local surjectivity. Kernels are sectionwise and cokernels are sheafified sectionwise cokernels, so this chase yields $\mathcal E\simeq\operatorname{coker}a$; no splitting of the original extension was asserted.

The source of $g$ is a constant finitely generated module sheaf, so the local-morphism lemma gives a further cover on which $g=\underline h$ for a linear map $h:K\to M$. On it, $a$ is the constant map $k\mapsto(-h(k),k)$ to $M\oplus B^t$. For the direct sum, the constant maps of the two inclusions and projections satisfy the biproduct identities because the constant-module functor is additive: these identities hold on the constant presheaves and hence after sheafification. They give the canonical isomorphism $\underline{M\oplus B^t}\simeq\underline M\oplus\underline{B^t}$. For the cokernel, apply sectionwise constant exactness to $0\to\operatorname{im}a_0\to M\oplus B^t\to P\to0$ and to $0\to\ker a_0\to K\to\operatorname{im}a_0\to0$, where $a_0(k)=(-h(k),k)$. The image of the constant map $a_0$ is thus the kernel of the constant quotient to $P$, which is sectionwise surjective. Consequently the presentation in step 5 becomes $\mathcal E\simeq\underline P$ with $P=(M\oplus B^t)/\{(-h(k),k):k\in K\}$. The images of generators of $M$ and the free basis generate $P$, so it is finitely generated. Degenerate members have zero restriction as in step 2. Bind the successive covers: this proves local constancy of finite type for $\mathcal E$ on every object of the original site and proves extension closure.
